target_customer: Creators who build custom GPTs in the OpenAI GPT Store and want to charge for them
problem: GPT Store creators lacked direct monetization and usage analytics. Top Road adds paywalls, subscriptions and analytics through a no code action.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers (Free, Pro 10 dollars a month, Business 90 dollars a month) plus a seller fee of 20 to 30 percent on creator revenue
product_category: Creator monetization and analytics for AI apps

founders.name: Celilsemi Sam Erkiner
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a full stack engineer who built 50+ apps; no education listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments through Stripe and an action that plugs into a GPT are standard web engineering; analytics on chats is the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: The product depends on OpenAI's GPT actions and OpenAI could ship native payments or analytics, which the press says creators had asked for.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: OpenAI announced GPT Store revenue sharing as a future program in January 2024 and ran an invite only US pilot; reports describe weak monetization on the store overall.

market_need_then: At the GPT Store launch in January 2024 builders complained of weak analytics and no payments, per VentureBeat and WIRED coverage; the company claims 300K dollars in subscription revenue enabled by January 2025.

identity.visual_style: Clean, simple, no code creator tool
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct; tagline Turn your GPT into a business

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing for GPT Builder Tools by Top Road; no wider community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Small two person team with a Product Hunt presence and a generic name; no brand press found. In a podcast the CEO joked the name sounds terrible, in an ambiguous remark.

outcome_analysis: Top Road is a two person team whose current product serves creators on OpenAI's GPT Store, a market the press describes as having weak monetization. It depends on a platform that could add the same payment and analytics features, and no outside funding was found. It remains listed as active, so the failure factor reflects structural risk, not a confirmed failure.
notes: YC lists batch Winter 2022 but a founded year of 2024 and the GPT Store product launched 2024 (Product Hunt lists 2024-09-04), so the original W22 idea is unknown and the batch era competition is not documented; the competitor list is empty for that reason. GetLatka says self funded; unverified. Founded year left null because of the conflict.
